data.title: bn-dip: operator workspace binding core
data.description: Review selection and durable operator-only binding core at exact HEAD. CLI integration and process-level F-28 witnesses remain pending. Assess: (1) can untrusted config grant authority, (2) can path or symlink substitution redirect reads/writes, (3) can malformed bindings bypass validation, (4) can failures leave an apparently valid partial binding, (5) do selection and crash behavior preserve invariants?

data.body: [severity:medium] init can successfully persist a binding that select will always reject. The encoded binding has no pre-write size check here, but select hard-limits binding reads to 1,048,576 bytes at lines 288-290. Because Vec<u8> engagements expand into JSON arrays, a syntactically and semantically valid declaration padded with TOML comments can exceed the read limit after encoding; init still atomically writes it and returns BoundWorkspace. A later select returns WorkspaceUnbound, and retrying init hits the existing scourge.toml O_EXCL at lines 218-225. Enforce the same bound before creating config, or store declarations compactly under a bounded source-size contract, and add a boundary plus restart test.

[severity:info] Five failure questions for this core slice: (1) Untrusted config cannot grant authority: Config accepts only version and workspace_id, and selected authority comes from the separately matched binding. (2) No confirmed path or symlink redirect in the core reads and writes: directory components and final files use NOFOLLOW, explicit paths are canonicalized, and hostile nested config fails closed; downstream authority-path execution is outside this slice and process-level F-28 remains pending. (3) Malformed bindings do not bypass validation: the file must be regular, owner-matched, mode-private, bounded, strict JSON, and consistent with version, workspace id, root, config digest, and revalidated engagements. (4) Interrupted config writes remain unbound and binding replacement follows file fsync, rename, and directory fsync, but the medium size-contract finding allows a successful init to create an apparently valid yet unselectable binding. (5) Selection and crash behavior otherwise preserve the reviewed invariants; no claim is made for pending CLI integration or process-level F-28.

data.reason: A valid oversized engagement can make init return success after writing a binding that select always rejects; align the write and read size contracts before approval.

data.body: [severity:high] The containment check compares the bare XDG state parent with the workspace root, while state_dir opens its scourge child. If the selected root is $XDG_STATE_HOME/scourge, both init here and select at lines 274-279 accept the same directory as the inspected tree and the authority store. This violates INV-21. Directory and file ownership, permissions, and the public config digest do not establish independent operator provenance when the tree itself is the authority store. Apply the containment check to the actual state directory before any config or binding access or publication, and cover equality and the state-child case with isolated temporary paths.

[severity:medium] Init durably publishes scourge.toml under an exclusive destination before binding serialization and publication can succeed. An interruption after config fsync or a later serialization or state-write error leaves select reporting WORKSPACE_UNBOUND and instructing the operator to rerun init, while that retry fails at O_EXCL. This also occurs independently of the size finding. Arrange publication or explicit recovery so interrupted init is safely retryable without replacing a pre-existing arbitrary config. Add a fault test that stops after the first file is published and then exercises the ordinary recovery route.

[severity:high] Authority does not constrain executable, evidence, or socket paths to absolute locators. Both init and select accept these values verbatim. A later consumer resolving a relative locator against CWD, or a bare executable through PATH, lets the inspected environment choose what the operator binding was meant to pin. These effects are pending CLI integration. Validate location semantics on both binding creation and readback, ideally requiring absolute paths or resolving against an independently trusted base, and test rejection before returning BoundWorkspace.

[severity:medium] Nearest-config discovery treats every stat error as absence through is_ok(). A denied lookup in a candidate directory can fall through to a bound ancestor, even though the code has not established that no nearer config exists. Advance only on explicit NotFound and otherwise return WORKSPACE_UNBOUND. Also require the opened config to be a regular file before reading any bytes, as already done for the binding. The hostile-tree test currently verifies unchanged foreign contents, which detects a write but cannot detect a read.

Independent exact-target review of the core. (1) Config admits only version and identity; the authority-origin guarantee fails if the selected tree and the state child coincide. (2) Directory-FD and NOFOLLOW patterns guard symlink substitution for opened files, with a remaining containment defect, an ambiguous discovery fallback, and unpinned relative authority locators. (3) Select validates binding ownership/mode, bounded decode, version, identity, root, digest and every stored engagement; relative locators currently bypass path validation. (4) The binding file uses temp, file fsync, rename and directory fsync; init can leave a durable, unrecoverable config or succeed with an oversized, unreadable binding. (5) Singleton and explicit two-engagement selection passed; recovery invariants still need a fix and fault test. Four focused tests and full just check passed on this commit with TMPDIR=/tmp and local test sockets enabled. CLI integration, process F-28 and orientation checks, and a production multi-engagement route remain pending.

data.reason: Core workspace binding has an operator-state containment gap, accepts relative authority locators, and can strand an unbound workspace or persist an oversized binding after successful init. Resolve the open threads and retarget before approval.

data.body: Fixed in d5a79d9: independent_state compares the actual state/scourge directory against the canonical workspace in both ancestor directions before config or binding reads/publication. overlap_rejected_in_both_directions and repro_overlap cover equality and nested paths.

Fixed in d5a79d9: init and select require absolute executable, evidence and socket paths and reject parent/current traversal. each_relative_locator_is_rejected_on_init_and_binding_readback exercises all three on creation and tampered readback.

Fixed in d5a79d9: a private, no-replace durable intent precedes binding and config publication; retries accept only byte-identical operator inputs and never replace unrelated files. Temp write, file fsync, rename-no-replace and directory fsync are used at each publication. retries_after_each_durable_publication_and_preserves_foreign_config injects failures after all three stages and checks retry and foreign preservation.

Fixed in d5a79d9: both serialized pending intent and final binding are bounded by the same LIMIT as the reader before either is published. bounded_encoding_rejects_before_publishing_and_smaller_input_survives_restart covers a large valid declaration, no config publication on rejection, and a smaller valid declaration on fresh selection.

Fixed in d5a79d9: discover_with advances only on NotFound and returns WORKSPACE_UNBOUND on other lookup errors; its injected permission-denial test verifies no ancestor lookup. select checks the opened no-follow config is regular before reading; fifo_config_is_never_read writes a witness to a FIFO and verifies the bytes remain after selection.

Static equality and ancestor cases are fixed and the existing regressions pass. [severity:high] The containment proof still depends on a separate name lookup. In workspace.rs:234-242, independent_state opens the state path without following symlinks, drops that descriptor, and then canonicalizes by name. Init and select later reopen the original name at lines 304 and 420. A mutable directory component in the inspected tree can change which pathname is compared independently of which directory supplies the authority file. Each no-follow open can pass while the separately canonicalized pathname describes a different location. Use the checked directory handle for binding access and ensure the containment comparison describes that same path or opened object. The overlap regression for select currently uses an empty store config, so rejection there alone does not witness the containment branch.

The normal interrupted-stage retries and foreign-config preservation pass. [severity:medium] Recovery omits durability after a rename that is visible but whose directory fsync failed or was interrupted. In workspace.rs:249-268, publish_same treats EEXIST plus matching bytes as success without flushing the existing entry. A retry can therefore return OK for a config or binding whose rename never became durable. The analogous mkdir EEXIST path at lines 162-169 skips syncing the state parent. Current hooks at lines 343 and 365-368 interrupt only after the publication helper returned. On matching retries, establish directory durability and exercise failures after rename and before or during that flush. Existing mismatched files and unsafe pending files also currently map to DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE via Io; distinguish an unusable binding or conflicting scope from an actual setup I/O failure.

Core containment still checks a separate pathname lookup from the authority directory access. An identical init retry can also accept renamed entries without establishing directory durability. CLI, process and multi-engagement acceptance remain pending.

data.body: Fixed in a373e6d: init and select open root and state once with NOFOLLOW, compare descriptor identities and both ancestry directions via opened parent handles, and use those same descriptors for config and binding operations. checked_state_handle_cannot_be_redirected_by_rename swaps the state name after validation for init and select; state_directory_moved_into_workspace_is_rejected_before_binding_access tests relocation before access. The ancestry checks are point-in-time; as with shared-custody filesystem access, they do not freeze an independently writable directory against later renames.

Fixed in a373e6d: existing state-parent mkdir, matching pending intent, matching binding and matching config all flush the relevant directory, and fsync errors propagate. retry_flush_failure_is_never_success_and_preserves_unrelated_state injects failure at each flush on both first attempt and retry, then verifies successful recovery and unrelated data preservation. Invalid or mismatching pending/config/binding data maps to WORKSPACE_UNBOUND.

Verified on a373e6d. Selection and setup compare opened directory identities and both ancestry directions, then use the same directory descriptors for config and authority accesses. The deterministic pathname replacement regression exercises both operations and confirms the replacement directory is unused. A separate regression relocates the opened state inside the opened workspace before the next check and verifies refusal with no binding or config publication. The ancestry check is point-in-time and does not freeze directory topology against a later move by an actor with write access.

Verified on a373e6d. Verified source paths call and propagate fsync for the state parent on mkdir success and EEXIST, the pending-intent directory on NOREPLACE success and EEXIST, and matching bindings and configs on retry. The deterministic fault test injects an error after each rename or mkdir and immediately before directory fsync on both attempts, verifies failure and unrelated-state preservation, and then exercises successful recovery. This verifies handling at the flush boundary rather than physical power-loss behavior. Mismatched or unusable private records map to WORKSPACE_UNBOUND, while actual flush errors propagate as I/O failures.

Approved the exact operator-binding core slice after descriptor-anchored containment and durable retry verification. All 17 focused tests, full just check with local sockets enabled, and git diff --check passed. CLI wiring, process-level F-28 and orientation, and the production multi-engagement route remain pending.

Approved the full bn-dip integration at bf645ce on base 8e64479. Reviewed operator authority isolation, descriptor-anchored point-in-time containment, bounded and durable init/add retry, explicit multi-engagement selection, and JSON/text/pretty behavior. Exact F-28 process test checks bound ancestor and blocked hostile nearest config, a live adapter/host sentinel, untouched credential/evidence FIFOs, and two responsive local endpoints with zero new connections. Leafless group help exits 0 before workspace dispatch and bare engagement remains a usage error. All 19 workspace, 7 CLI, and 6 workspace-process tests, full just check, and diff check passed. Teapot sibling files and Cargo.lock match base. The optional pinned live Teapot test remained ignored.
